items.title: Cursor agents gain Computer Use to control desktop apps including iOS Simulator
facts: Cursor can now control your computer. Agents can drive desktop apps like the iOS Simulator to test the features they build.
Computer Use lets agents click and type across any app on your computer, not just the browser.
Cursor uses it on its own when a task needs it. You can also ask for it by @-mentioning Computer Use in your prompt.
The feature is available by updating the desktop app; Cursor announced no accompanying pricing change.

x_posts.author: @ondrejposts
x_posts.text:
Cursor agents can now control your computer.

Sounds like a gimmick until you see what it's for: the agent builds a feature, opens the iOS Simulator, clicks through it and checks it actually works.

For a freelancer that's the expensive part of every job. Writing code was already fast. Testing it by hand before the client sees it was not.

Write, run, check in one loop. Closest thing yet to handing off a whole ticket.

items.reaction: A freelancer noted that the feature addresses the costly manual testing step after fast code generation, enabling a write-run-check loop for handing off complete tickets.

items.title: Claude Code CLI adds MCP Tasks and Elicitations for long-running jobs and mid-task input
facts: We’re adding support for MCP Tasks and Elicitations in Claude. Tasks let Claude give plugins long-running jobs such as deep research and report back when they’re done.
Elicitations let plugins ask users for input mid-task, such as confirming a refund or filling in a missing detail.
Tasks and Elicitations are available today in the Claude Code CLI, rolling out to more Claude products soon.
MCP tasks are in public beta in the Claude Code CLI and require Claude Code v2.1.304 or later.

items.title: Creator of Claude Code desktop announces departure from Anthropic
facts: Yesterday was my last day at Anthropic. I created Claude Code on desktop because I believe everyone can be a builder.
Every feature request and bug report we got from this community was a gift that impacted millions of lives.
Walking away from my best friends, a product I poured my heart into, and the mission was the hardest thing I’ve done in my career.
I'm already itching to get back to addressing all your feedback. I'll share what's next soon!

x_posts.author: @amorriscode
x_posts.text:
Yesterday was my last day at Anthropic.
 
I created Claude Code on desktop because I believe everyone can be a builder. Every feature request and bug report we got from this community was a gift that impacted millions of lives. I’m eternally grateful for those gifts, the product wouldn’t be what it is without you.
 
Anthropic is doing some of the most important work of our time. Contributing to that mission will forever be a career highlight for me. I never imagined I’d get to contribute to something so special in my lifetime.

Walking away from my best friends, a product I poured my heart into, and the mission was the hardest thing I’ve done in my career. But now I have some free time for GTA VI.

I'm already itching to get back to addressing all your feedback. I'll share what's next soon!
